preheader: US national debt hits $40T, Oura delays IPO, and UCI researchers warn of ChatGPT's effect on your brain.

lead.headline: US Gross National Debt Crosses $40 Trillion Mark
lead.body: The gross national debt of the United States crossed the $40 trillion threshold in August, continuing a rapid upward trajectory. The nation's debt is currently climbing by $1 trillion every five months, while the federal deficit has already reached $2 trillion with a month still remaining in the fiscal year.
lead.why: Understanding the national debt and deficit is crucial for your macroeconomics classes, and it helps you anticipate how government borrowing might affect interest rates and your future investment portfolios.

stories.headline: Three in Four Americans Fear a Stock Market Correction is Coming
stories.body: A new survey reveals that 75% of Americans believe recent stock market gains are unsustainable and that a correction may be on the horizon. This caution comes even as the S&P 500 trades near record highs, up about 13% on the year.
stories.why: As you look to start your own investment portfolio, this widespread caution suggests you should study defensive investing strategies and watch how market sentiment shifts.

stories.headline: Chick-fil-A CEO Andrew Cathy Focuses on International Growth
stories.body: Chick-fil-A is expanding its footprint into new international markets, including Singapore, under CEO Andrew Cathy. Despite the global push, Cathy emphasizes that the family-owned business intends to stay true to its roots.
stories.why: This is a prime case study for your business administration classes on how private, family-owned enterprises scale globally without losing their core brand identity.

stories.headline: AI Wearables Face Privacy Backlash as Oura Delays Public Debut
stories.body: Tech giants like Apple, Google, and Meta are pushing new AI-powered wearable devices, but growing consumer privacy concerns are triggering a public backlash. Amid these rising concerns, health-tech wearable company Oura has delayed its planned IPO.
stories.why: If you want to launch a tech startup, this shows that user privacy and public trust are just as critical to your valuation and IPO timeline as the technology itself.

stories.headline: OpenAI Safety Systems Lead Resigns Over Dangerous Work Culture
stories.body: David Robinson, the safety systems lead at OpenAI, has publicly resigned from his role. In an essay for The Atlantic, Robinson warned that the company behind ChatGPT fosters a dangerous culture and does not take enough care with rapid AI development.
stories.why: Keeping tabs on executive departures at top AI firms helps you assess which platforms are stable and ethically sound enough to build your future business tools upon.

stories.headline: Consulting Firms Warn Cheap AI Models Will Strain the Power Grid
stories.body: New reports from McKinsey and Boston Consulting Group reveal that falling AI token prices are driving companies to use the technology more. This surge in actual corporate usage is projected to put massive pressure on the electric grid.
stories.why: This highlights a major infrastructure challenge that consulting firms are actively tackling, giving you a great talking point for future networking and case interviews.

stories.headline: BCG Executive Warns of Cognitive Decline From Passive AI Habits
stories.body: The global lead of people and organization at Boston Consulting Group warned that relying too heavily on AI tools poses an existential risk of deskilling. He highlighted two specific habits that can weaken critical thinking and cause cognitive skills to atrophy.
stories.why: As a business student, you must learn to use AI as an active collaborator rather than a passive replacement to ensure your own analytical skills stay sharp for competitive consulting roles.

stories.headline: UCI Researchers Find Passive Chatbot Use Blunts Critical Thinking
stories.body: A research team at UC Irvine partnered with McGraw Hill to analyze ten years of student usage data from the learning platform Aleks. The study concluded that passive reliance on chatbots can blunt students' critical thinking skills unless they actively change how they interact with the technology.

stories.headline: Top Seeds Rybakina and Sabalenka Suffer Shock Defeats at China Open
stories.body: The China Open lost its top two seeds in early rounds. World No. 1 Elena Rybakina was ousted in the second round by unseeded Alina Charaeva, 3-6, 6-4, 6-3, while No. 2 seed Aryna Sabalenka was swept in straight sets by 34th-ranked Nikola Bartunkova in the third round.

term.name: Stock market correction
term.definition: A stock market correction is a decline of 10% or more in a stock market index from its most recent peak. It is often viewed as a natural way for the market to cool down after unsustainable gains, which three in four Americans currently believe are happening with the S&P 500.

serve.headline: Six climate tech startups secured funding at the Opalene Climate Challenge
serve.body: Six climate tech startups won funding at a Washington event designed to help companies that do not directly feed AI data centers, as venture capital increasingly shifts toward AI infrastructure. The challenge was created to support climate innovations that are facing longer waits for traditional investment.
